where: Section 2, the FB = BB ± 180° formula line
problem: The rule that tells the reader which sign to use is cut off: it reads "use + when BB  180°." The two cases are missing, so a student cannot apply the formula and may add 180° to a bearing over 180° and get a value above 360°.
fix: use + when BB < 180° (answer stays below 360°) and − when BB > 180°.

where: Figure node f (back-check note) and Quiz Q2 answer
problem: "FB − BB = 180°" is not true as written: the difference is +180° for one direction of travel and −180° for the other, so the line fails its own check half the time. The chapter text itself uses the magnitude in worked example 1, step 1.
fix: Write the check as |FB − BB| = 180°, or FB = BB ± 180°. In Quiz Q2 answer use: the fore and back bearings of every line differ by 180° (magnitude).

problem: The reasoning calls the result "the interior angle" although PQ and PR do not form a polygon; a student may carry the polygon rule to a case where there is no inside or outside.
fix: The angle QPR is simply the smaller angle between the two directions: 250°00′ − 120°00′ = 130°00′, which is under 180°, so it is taken as it stands; if the difference had exceeded 180°, the angle would be 360° minus that difference.
